notes: Maps every ISO 27001:2013 Annex A clause referenced by a Prism connector check to the corresponding control in each other seeded framework. Curated 2026-09-09 from the published informative mappings cited per entry. Frameworks with no defensible correspondence for a clause are omitted for that clause (empty arrays are invalid). DPDPA is NOT a target here — connector checks carry their own dpdpaControlAreas and DPDPA matches on control_area. AWSWAF / AZUREWAF are architecture reviews, not control catalogues, and are intentionally uncovered. control_reference strings match the bare-ref normalisation the framework import pipeline writes to question_framework_controls (see api/src/routes/frameworks.js).

GDPR.rationale: Separating conflicting duties limits the ability of a single actor to compromise confidentiality or integrity of processing.

SOC2.rationale: The entity selects control activities, including segregation of incompatible duties, to mitigate risks.

HIPAA.rationale: Information-access-management policies must separate authorization, establishment and modification of access.

CIS.rationale: Define and maintain role-based access control so no single role holds conflicting privileges.

PCIDSS.rationale: An access-control model assigns privileges by job classification and function.

GDPR.rationale: A mobile-device policy is an organisational measure protecting personal data processed off-premises.

SOC2.rationale: The entity restricts the transmission, movement and removal of information to authorised users and protects it on mobile devices.

HIPAA.rationale: Device and media controls govern receipt and removal of hardware holding ePHI.

CIS.rationale: Encrypt data on end-user devices, including portable and mobile devices.

PCIDSS.rationale: Usage policies define acceptable use and location of end-user technologies.

GDPR.rationale: Knowing which assets process personal data underpins the record of processing activities.

SOC2.rationale: The entity identifies and manages the inventory of information assets as a basis for logical access security.

HIPAA.rationale: Maintaining a record of hardware and media movements requires an asset inventory.

CIS.rationale: Establish and maintain a detailed enterprise asset inventory.

PCIDSS.rationale: Maintain an inventory of system components in scope for PCI DSS.

SOC2.rationale: Accountability for information assets is assigned to enable control operation.

HIPAA.rationale: Assigned security responsibility identifies the person accountable for policies and procedures.

CIS.rationale: The enterprise asset inventory records an owner for each asset.

PCIDSS.rationale: The component inventory records the function and owner of each in-scope asset.

GDPR.rationale: Classifying information by sensitivity drives the risk-appropriate level of protection for personal data.

SOC2.rationale: The entity identifies and maintains confidential information to meet its confidentiality objectives.

HIPAA.rationale: The risk analysis must identify where ePHI is created, received, maintained or transmitted.

CIS.rationale: Establish and maintain a data classification scheme.

PCIDSS.rationale: Media is classified so the sensitivity of the data can be determined.

GDPR.rationale: Procedures for handling assets — including encryption of stored data — protect personal data at rest.

SOC2.rationale: The entity protects information assets during storage through access restriction and encryption.

HIPAA.rationale: Encryption and decryption is an addressable control for ePHI at rest.

CIS.rationale: Encrypt sensitive data at rest.

PCIDSS.rationale: Primary account numbers are rendered unreadable wherever stored.

GDPR.rationale: An access-control policy enforces the integrity and confidentiality principle.

SOC2.rationale: The entity implements logical access security measures over protected information assets.

HIPAA.rationale: Information-access-management policies authorise access to ePHI.

CIS.rationale: Establish and maintain an access-granting process.

PCIDSS.rationale: Processes and mechanisms for restricting access by business need to know are defined.

A.9.1.2.title: Access to networks and network services

GDPR.rationale: Restricting network-service access limits exposure of systems processing personal data.

SOC2.rationale: The entity implements boundary-protection controls over network access from outside its boundaries.

HIPAA.rationale: Technical access controls allow access only to authorised persons or software.

CIS.rationale: Establish and maintain a secure network architecture.

PCIDSS.rationale: Inbound traffic to the cardholder data environment is restricted to that which is necessary.

SOC2.rationale: The entity registers and authorises users before granting access, and removes access when no longer required.

HIPAA.rationale: Access-authorisation procedures govern granting access to ePHI.

CIS.rationale: Establish and maintain an inventory of accounts.

PCIDSS.rationale: All users are assigned a unique ID before access to system components is allowed.

SOC2.rationale: The entity authorises, modifies or removes access to data and systems based on roles and responsibilities.

HIPAA.rationale: Access-establishment-and-modification procedures provision user access to ePHI.

CIS.rationale: Grant access rights through a defined process on hire or role change.

PCIDSS.rationale: Access is assigned based on job classification and least privilege.

GDPR.rationale: Constraining privileged accounts reduces the risk of unauthorised access to personal data.

SOC2.rationale: The entity restricts privileged logical access to authorised personnel.

HIPAA.rationale: Workforce-security controls limit access to those whose role requires it, including privileged roles.

CIS.rationale: Restrict administrator privileges to dedicated administrator accounts.

PCIDSS.rationale: Privileged access is assigned and reviewed for system and application accounts.

A.9.2.4.title: Management of secret authentication information of users

GDPR.rationale: Protecting credentials and secrets safeguards access to systems processing personal data.

SOC2.rationale: The entity manages credentials and authentication secrets for identified users.

HIPAA.rationale: Password-management procedures govern creating, changing and safeguarding passwords.

CIS.rationale: Use unique passwords for all enterprise assets.

PCIDSS.rationale: Strong authentication for users and administrators is managed with defined factors.

GDPR.rationale: Periodic access reviews evidence the accountability principle for personal-data access.

SOC2.rationale: The entity reviews access rights periodically for appropriateness.

HIPAA.rationale: Access is reviewed and modified as part of access establishment and modification.

CIS.rationale: Establish and maintain a process to revoke access when no longer required, informed by review.

PCIDSS.rationale: All user accounts and access privileges are reviewed at least once every six months.

A.9.2.6.title: Removal or adjustment of access rights

SOC2.rationale: The entity removes access to data and systems when no longer required or upon termination.

HIPAA.rationale: Termination procedures end access to ePHI when employment ends.

CIS.rationale: Disable dormant accounts.

PCIDSS.rationale: Access for terminated users is immediately revoked.

GDPR.rationale: Restricting information access by default enforces data-protection by design and by default.

SOC2.rationale: The entity restricts logical access to information based on need.

HIPAA.rationale: Technical policies restrict access to ePHI to authorised persons and software.

CIS.rationale: Configure data-access control lists based on need to know.

PCIDSS.rationale: Access is limited to the least privileges necessary to perform job responsibilities.

GDPR.rationale: Secure authentication, including multi-factor, is a measure ensuring ongoing confidentiality of processing.

SOC2.rationale: The entity uses authentication mechanisms, including MFA, to control logical access.

HIPAA.rationale: Person-or-entity authentication verifies that a user seeking access is who they claim to be.

CIS.rationale: Require MFA for externally-exposed applications.

PCIDSS.rationale: MFA is implemented for all access into the cardholder data environment.

CERTIN.rationale: Secure and authenticated access to ICT systems must be maintained.

SOC2.rationale: The entity enforces password quality and lifecycle through a management system.

HIPAA.rationale: Procedures for creating, changing and safeguarding passwords are implemented.

CIS.rationale: Enforce minimum password length and uniqueness across enterprise assets.

PCIDSS.rationale: Minimum password length and complexity requirements are enforced.

SOC2.rationale: The entity restricts the installation and use of unauthorised or privileged software.

HIPAA.rationale: Integrity controls protect ePHI from improper alteration by privileged utilities.

CIS.rationale: Allowlist authorised software and block unauthorised utilities.

PCIDSS.rationale: Only necessary services, protocols and daemons are enabled.

A.10.1.1.title: Policy on the use of cryptographic controls

GDPR.rationale: A cryptographic-controls policy governs risk-appropriate encryption and pseudonymisation of personal data.

SOC2.rationale: The entity protects information during transmission, movement and storage using approved cryptographic safeguards.

HIPAA.rationale: Encryption and decryption is an addressable technical safeguard for electronic protected health information.

CIS.rationale: Encrypt data on end-user devices according to an enterprise encryption standard.

PCIDSS.rationale: Stored account data is rendered unreadable using strong cryptography.

CERTIN.rationale: Approved cryptographic controls support secure and authenticated access to ICT systems.

GDPR.rationale: Effective key management is intrinsic to the encryption of personal data.

SOC2.rationale: The entity manages cryptographic keys over their lifecycle to protect information.

HIPAA.rationale: Encryption of ePHI depends on protected key generation, storage and rotation.

CIS.rationale: Encrypt sensitive data at rest using managed keys.

PCIDSS.rationale: Key-management policies and procedures cover key generation, distribution and rotation.

SOC2.rationale: The entity documents and communicates the procedures needed to operate its controls.

HIPAA.rationale: Policies and procedures are implemented and maintained in written form.

CIS.rationale: Establish and maintain a documented secure configuration process.

PCIDSS.rationale: An information-security policy is documented, published and disseminated.

GDPR.rationale: Controlled change keeps data-protection measures effective as systems evolve.

SOC2.rationale: The entity authorises, designs, tests and approves changes to infrastructure and software.

HIPAA.rationale: Periodic evaluation covers environmental and operational changes affecting ePHI security.

CIS.rationale: Configuration changes are managed through the secure configuration process.

PCIDSS.rationale: Changes to system components follow documented change-control procedures.

GDPR.rationale: Anti-malware controls preserve the integrity and availability of systems processing personal data.

SOC2.rationale: The entity implements controls to prevent or detect and act upon malicious software.

HIPAA.rationale: Protection from malicious software is an addressable security-awareness control.

CIS.rationale: Deploy and maintain anti-malware software.

PCIDSS.rationale: An anti-malware solution is deployed on all system components at risk.

GDPR.rationale: The ability to restore availability and access to personal data in a timely manner depends on backups.

SOC2.rationale: The entity maintains and tests backup processes to meet availability commitments.

HIPAA.rationale: A data-backup plan creates and maintains retrievable exact copies of ePHI.

CIS.rationale: Perform automated backups of in-scope enterprise assets.

GDPR.rationale: Logging user and administrator activity supports detecting unauthorised processing of personal data.

SOC2.rationale: The entity monitors system components for anomalies through event logging.

HIPAA.rationale: Audit controls record and examine activity in systems containing ePHI.

CIS.rationale: Collect audit logs from enterprise assets.

PCIDSS.rationale: Audit logs capture the events needed to reconstruct activity.

CERTIN.rationale: Logs of ICT systems must be enabled and maintained.

SOC2.rationale: Logging infrastructure and its records are protected from tampering to support reliable monitoring.

HIPAA.rationale: Integrity controls protect audit records from improper alteration or destruction.

CIS.rationale: Ensure adequate audit-log storage and protect logs from alteration.

PCIDSS.rationale: Audit-log files are protected to prevent modification.

A.12.5.1.title: Installation of software on operational systems

SOC2.rationale: Software deployed to production is authorised and controlled.

HIPAA.rationale: Controlling software installation protects ePHI integrity on operational systems.

CIS.rationale: Allowlist authorised software so only approved software runs.

PCIDSS.rationale: Security vulnerabilities are managed for bespoke, custom and third-party software.

GDPR.rationale: Administrator activity logs provide evidence that the controller can demonstrate accountability.

SOC2.rationale: The entity monitors system components and privileged activity for anomalous events.

HIPAA.rationale: Audit controls record and examine activity in systems containing electronic protected health information.

CIS.rationale: Collect audit logs, including privileged administrative activity, across enterprise assets.

PCIDSS.rationale: Audit logs capture actions taken by individuals with administrative access.

CERTIN.rationale: ICT system logs must be maintained securely and made available for incident response.

GDPR.rationale: A process to regularly test and remediate vulnerabilities evaluates the effectiveness of security measures.

SOC2.rationale: The entity identifies and manages vulnerabilities through detection and monitoring.

HIPAA.rationale: Risk-management measures reduce vulnerabilities to a reasonable level.

CIS.rationale: Establish and maintain a vulnerability-management process.

PCIDSS.rationale: Security vulnerabilities are identified and assigned a risk ranking.

CERTIN.rationale: Vulnerabilities and their remediation must be tracked for reporting.

GDPR.rationale: Network segmentation and filtering protect the confidentiality of personal data in transit and at the boundary.

SOC2.rationale: The entity implements boundary protections to restrict network access.

HIPAA.rationale: Transmission-security controls guard ePHI over networks.

CIS.rationale: Establish and maintain a secure network architecture.

PCIDSS.rationale: Network security controls are implemented between trusted and untrusted networks.

GDPR.rationale: Network segregation limits the blast radius of a compromise affecting personal data.

SOC2.rationale: The entity implements boundary protection to segregate and restrict access between network segments.

HIPAA.rationale: Technical access controls include isolating systems that store or transmit ePHI.

CIS.rationale: Establish and maintain a secure network architecture using segmentation.

PCIDSS.rationale: System components in a trusted network are segmented from untrusted networks.

GDPR.rationale: Encryption of personal data in transit protects it during transfer between parties and systems.

SOC2.rationale: The entity protects information during transmission and movement.

HIPAA.rationale: Encryption is an addressable transmission-security control for ePHI in transit.

CIS.rationale: Encrypt sensitive data in transit.

PCIDSS.rationale: Strong cryptography protects cardholder data during transmission over open networks.

SOC2.rationale: Information sent via electronic messaging is protected in transit.

HIPAA.rationale: Transmission-security controls apply to ePHI sent by electronic messaging.

CIS.rationale: Use DNS filtering and email security services to protect messaging.

PCIDSS.rationale: PANs are never sent by end-user messaging technologies without strong cryptography.

A.14.1.2.title: Securing application services on public networks

GDPR.rationale: Application services traversing public networks must protect the confidentiality and integrity of personal data against interception and modification.

SOC2.rationale: The entity restricts the transmission of information over public networks and protects it with encryption and application-layer controls.

HIPAA.rationale: Transmission security safeguards ePHI transmitted over an electronic communications network.

CIS.rationale: Deploy an application-layer firewall / WAF to inspect and filter traffic to public-facing applications.

PCIDSS.rationale: Public-facing web applications are protected against attacks by an automated technical solution that detects and prevents web-based attacks.

CERTIN.rationale: CERT-In guidelines require WAF protection and TLS for public-facing applications.

GDPR.rationale: Transaction integrity controls prevent incomplete transmission, mis-routing, and unauthorised message alteration of personal data.

SOC2.rationale: The entity protects information during transmission, including the integrity of application transactions.

HIPAA.rationale: Integrity controls protect ePHI from improper alteration or destruction, including in transit.

CIS.rationale: Leverage vetted modules and enforce input/output validation for application transactions.

PCIDSS.rationale: Software engineering techniques prevent or mitigate common attacks against application transactions (injection, tampering).

GDPR.rationale: Change control keeps privacy safeguards intact through the development lifecycle.

SOC2.rationale: Changes to applications and infrastructure follow a controlled process.

HIPAA.rationale: Technical evaluation follows changes that affect the security of ePHI.

CIS.rationale: Establish and maintain a secure application-development process.

PCIDSS.rationale: Significant changes are followed by verification that applicable controls remain in place.

GDPR.rationale: Data protection by design and by default is engineered into systems from the outset.

SOC2.rationale: Secure design principles are applied when developing and configuring systems.

CIS.rationale: Establish and maintain a secure application-development process incorporating secure-design standards.

PCIDSS.rationale: Bespoke and custom software is developed securely, based on industry standards and secure design.

A.15.1.1.title: Information security policy for supplier relationships

GDPR.rationale: Controllers use only processors providing sufficient guarantees of appropriate security measures.

SOC2.rationale: The entity assesses and manages risks arising from vendors and business partners.

HIPAA.rationale: Business-associate contracts require safeguards for ePHI handled by third parties.

CIS.rationale: Establish and maintain an inventory of service providers.

PCIDSS.rationale: Written agreements with third-party service providers acknowledge their security responsibilities.

A.15.2.1.title: Monitoring and review of supplier services

GDPR.rationale: The processor makes available information for, and contributes to, audits by the controller.

SOC2.rationale: The entity monitors the performance of vendors against commitments and requirements.

HIPAA.rationale: The covered entity obtains assurances that business associates safeguard ePHI on an ongoing basis.

CIS.rationale: Assess service providers according to the enterprise's service-provider management policy.

PCIDSS.rationale: A programme monitors third-party service providers' PCI DSS compliance status at least annually.

GDPR.rationale: Personal-data breaches are notified to the supervisory authority without undue delay.

SOC2.rationale: The entity evaluates security events to determine whether they could result in a failure to meet objectives.

HIPAA.rationale: Security incidents are identified, reported and responded to.

CIS.rationale: Establish and maintain contact information and a process for reporting incidents.

PCIDSS.rationale: Specific personnel are designated to be available to respond to suspected or confirmed incidents.

CERTIN.rationale: Cyber incidents must be reported to CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing.

A.16.1.4.title: Assessment of and decision on information security events

GDPR.rationale: The controller assesses whether a breach is likely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of individuals.

SOC2.rationale: The entity responds to identified security incidents by executing a defined incident-response programme.

HIPAA.rationale: Response and reporting includes assessing the harmful effects of security incidents.

CIS.rationale: Establish and maintain an incident-response process that classifies and prioritises events.

PCIDSS.rationale: Personnel responsible for responding to incidents are appropriately trained.

CERTIN.rationale: Incident classification informs the mandatory 6-hour report to CERT-In.

GDPR.rationale: Where a breach is high risk, affected data subjects are informed without undue delay as part of the response.

SOC2.rationale: The entity contains, remediates and recovers from security incidents per its response programme.

HIPAA.rationale: The entity mitigates, to the extent practicable, harmful effects of known security incidents.

CIS.rationale: Conduct routine incident-response exercises and refine the process.

PCIDSS.rationale: The incident-response plan is reviewed and tested at least annually.

CERTIN.rationale: Entities must provide information and assistance to CERT-In during incident response.

A.18.1.1.title: Identification of applicable legislation and contractual requirements

GDPR.rationale: The controller identifies its legal obligations and implements measures to demonstrate compliance.

SOC2.rationale: The entity identifies and assesses external legal and regulatory requirements relevant to its objectives.

HIPAA.rationale: Reasonable and appropriate policies are implemented to comply with the standards and implementation specifications.

PCIDSS.rationale: An overall information-security policy addresses applicable legal and regulatory requirements.

GDPR.rationale: Records are retained no longer than necessary and protected against loss for the retention period.

SOC2.rationale: Records including audit history are retained and protected to support monitoring and investigation.

HIPAA.rationale: Documentation is retained for six years from creation or last effective date.

CIS.rationale: Retain audit logs for a defined, adequate period.

PCIDSS.rationale: Audit-log history is retained for at least 12 months, with 3 months immediately available.

CERTIN.rationale: Logs must be maintained securely for a rolling period of 180 days within Indian jurisdiction.

A.18.1.4.title: Privacy and protection of personally identifiable information

GDPR.rationale: Personal data is processed in a manner ensuring appropriate security, including protection against unauthorised processing.

SOC2.rationale: The entity limits the use of personal information to the purposes identified in its privacy notice.

HIPAA.rationale: Administrative, technical and physical safeguards protect the privacy of protected health information.

CIS.rationale: Establish and maintain a data-management process covering sensitive and personal data.

A.18.2.2.title: Compliance with security policies and standards

GDPR.rationale: A process for regularly testing, assessing and evaluating the effectiveness of security measures.

SOC2.rationale: The entity evaluates whether controls are present and functioning through ongoing and separate evaluations.

HIPAA.rationale: Periodic technical and non-technical evaluation establishes the extent to which controls meet requirements.

CIS.rationale: Managed configuration standards are reviewed and enforced against a documented baseline.

PCIDSS.rationale: Responsibility is assigned for monitoring compliance with the information-security programme.
